---
title: "Join two tables"
---

This example adds each order's customer details from a second table.

Prerequisites: PHP 8.3 or later and `composer require phpstats/phplyr`. The pipe version needs PHP 8.5. See [Installation](../getting-started.qmd#installation).

Both tables are created inline. Save the script as `example.php` in the
project directory and run `php example.php`.

{{< include pages/_join.md >}}

`left_join()` keeps every row of the left table, `orders`, and adds the
columns of `customers` from the row with the same `customer_id`. Customer
c1 has two orders, so both rows get Ana's details. Order 4's customer, c9, is
not in `customers`, so its `name` and `city` are NA. Customer c3 has no
orders and does not appear. The result keeps the left table's row order.

`inner_join()` would drop order 4, and `full_join()` would also add a row
for c3. [Joins, binding, and set operations](../reference/two-table.qmd#joins)
describes the other joins, their options, and `join_by()` for joins on
differently named columns and inequalities.
